rules.explanation: Under Section 15 of the MSMED Act 2006, the payment period agreed in writing between buyer and supplier shall not exceed 45 days from acceptance or deemed acceptance.

Where no payment period is agreed in writing, Section 15 mandates payment before the appointed day. Under Section 2(b), the appointed day is the day following immediately after the expiry of 15 days from acceptance or deemed acceptance.
Under Section 2(b) Explanation (ii), if no objection is made in writing by the buyer regarding goods or services within 15 days of delivery, deemed acceptance occurs on the actual day of delivery.
Section 16 mandates penal compound interest at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India on delayed payments from the appointed day or agreed due date.
Section 16 specifies that the interest payable by the buyer shall compound with monthly rests.

rules.legal_reference: MSMED Act 2006, Section 2(n) and MSME Notification S.O. 2119(E) dated 26 June 2020
rules.explanation: Statutory delayed payment remedies under Chapter V of the MSMED Act 2006 apply strictly to micro and small enterprises. Medium enterprises are excluded from Section 2(n) supplier protections for Chapter V.

rules.legal_reference: MSMED Act 2006, Section 2(n) & Section 8(1); Ministry of MSME Notification S.O. 2119(E)
rules.explanation: To qualify as an eligible 'supplier' under Section 2(n), filing a memorandum (Udyam Registration) under Section 8(1) is mandatory.

rules.legal_reference: Supreme Court of India, Silpi Industries etc. v. Kerala State Road Transport Corporation & Anr., 2021 SCC OnLine SC 439
rules.explanation: The Supreme Court ruled that in order to claim benefits under Chapter V of the MSMED Act 2006, the supplier must have held valid registration on or before the date of supply of goods or services. Registration cannot operate retrospectively.

rules.legal_reference: Reserve Bank of India Bank Rate under Section 49 of RBI Act, 1934
rules.explanation: Current Bank Rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India under Section 49 of the RBI Act is 5.75% per annum, verified directly on the official RBI portal.

rules.legal_reference: Ministry of MSME OM No. UAM/MC/01/2017-SME (15 Dec 2017) & OM No. 5/2(2)/2021-E/P&G/Policy (2 July 2021)
rules.explanation: Under MSMED Act Section 2(n), statutory protections apply to enterprises engaged in manufacture or rendering services. The 2017 OM explicitly excluded trading activities (NIC 45-47). The 2 July 2021 OM permitted retail/wholesale traders to register on Udyam solely for Priority Sector Lending, excluding Chapter V delayed payments. Due to divergent judicial interpretations across High Courts, this rule remains unverified until current legal requirements and case applicability are confirmed.
